checklist.step: Inventory every statutory and OSFI-directed filing obligation
actions: Open the Regulatory Obligations module and list every obligation the Insurance Companies Act, OSFI guidelines and the company's by-laws create, including the annual return, quarterly LICAT/MCT returns, the appointed actuary's report and the AGM notice cycle.
For each obligation record the authority (OSFI, provincial regulator, corporate by-law), the governing section (e.g. ss. 357-358, 368, 369) and the owning role.
Confirm with the Appointed Actuary and Corporate Secretary that no obligation affecting their function is missing from the inventory.
Save the inventory as the baseline obligations register for the fiscal year.
checklist.done: every statutory and OSFI-directed obligation is listed with authority, section and owning role in the register.

checklist.step: Map each obligation to its owning role and system of record
actions: For each register row, assign a named preparer and a named reviewer distinct from the preparer.
Record the system used to submit or evidence the filing (Internal Regulatory System for OSFI returns, board portal for AGM/board materials).
Confirm each preparer's access to the assigned system is active before the fiscal year's first due date.
Circulate the assignment list to the Chief Risk Officer for acknowledgement.
checklist.done: every obligation has a named preparer, reviewer and system of record acknowledged by the Chief Risk Officer.

checklist.step: Compute due dates and internal lead times for each obligation
actions: Pull the statutory or OSFI-instructed due date for each obligation (e.g. the prescribed period after fiscal year-end for the annual return, the 21-days-before-the-annual-meeting deadline for board reporting under s. 357-358).
Back off internal milestones: draft-complete date, actuarial/financial sign-off date, and final review date.
Enter the due date and each milestone into the calendar record.
Flag any obligation whose lead time is shorter than the internal minimum (10 business days) for manager review.
checklist.done: every obligation carries a due date and internal milestone dates consistent with the governing statute or instruction.

checklist.step: Build the master filing calendar entry in the GRC platform
actions: In the GRC platform, create a workflow record per obligation with fields for authority, citation, due date, preparer, reviewer and status.
Link each record to its prior-year submission evidence for reference.
Set the record status to 'Open' and route it into the current fiscal year's calendar view.
Have the Regulatory Reporting Manager spot-check 10% of new records for field completeness before publishing the calendar.
checklist.done: the calendar view in the GRC platform shows every obligation as an open, fully-populated record.

checklist.step: Configure automated deadline reminders
actions: Enable T-60/T-30/T-10 alert rules against each obligation's due date, addressed to the preparer and reviewer.
Add a dedicated T-21-days alert on every board/AGM reporting item to enforce the s. 357-358 notice window.
Test-fire one alert per rule type and confirm delivery to the assigned mailbox.
Escalate to the Regulatory Reporting Manager any alert rule that fails to fire in testing.
checklist.done: every obligation has active, verified reminder rules including the dedicated AGM T-21-day alert.

checklist.step: Track OSFI annual return preparation through to submission
actions: In the Internal Regulatory System open the annual return template for the current fiscal year and populate it from the Controller's trial balance and the Appointed Actuary's valuation figures.
Route the draft to the Controller and Chief Financial Officer for review and sign-off.
Submit the finalized return and capture the system-generated confirmation number.
Post the confirmation number and submission date onto the calendar record.
checklist.done: the annual return is submitted with a captured confirmation number logged against its calendar record.

checklist.step: Track the appointed actuary's report to CEO, CFO and directors
actions: Confirm the annual report addressing the financial condition of the company under s. 368 is drafted and delivered to the CEO and CFO ahead of the calendar due date.
Where the report identifies a matter with material adverse effect requiring rectification under s. 369, confirm escalation to the directors and, if unresolved, to the Superintendent is logged.
File the delivered report and any escalation memo in the calendar record's evidence link.
Notify the Regulatory Reporting Manager once delivery is confirmed.
checklist.done: the actuary's s. 368 report and any s. 369 escalation are delivered, filed and confirmed to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.

checklist.step: Track the AGM notice and board reporting cycle
actions: In the board portal confirm the annual meeting date is set and the 21-day notice window is calculated backward from it.
Upload the appointed actuary's report and any director-facing financial condition materials to the board portal ahead of the 21-day deadline.
Record the actual notice-issued date against the calendar's T-21-day milestone.
Flag to the Regulatory Reporting Manager any notice issued inside the 21-day window.
checklist.done: the AGM notice and supporting board materials are issued at or before 21 days before the meeting, with the date logged.

checklist.step: Log actual completion dates against due dates
actions: For each closed obligation, enter the actual submission or delivery date into the calendar record.
Auto-calculate the variance (days early/late) and colour-code any negative variance red.
Attach the submission confirmation or delivered document to the record.
Close the record status to 'Filed' only once the evidence attachment is present.
checklist.done: every closed obligation shows actual vs due date variance and a filed evidence attachment.

checklist.step: Escalate late or at-risk obligations
actions: Run the at-risk report weekly for any obligation inside its T-10 window with status still 'Open'.
Contact the assigned preparer for a completion estimate and record it on the calendar.
Where completion cannot be reached before the due date, escalate to the Chief Risk Officer in writing the same business day.
Record the escalation outcome and any regulator contact made to explain the delay.
checklist.done: every at-risk obligation is escalated before its due date with a recorded outcome.

checklist.step: Reconcile the calendar to the full obligations register quarterly
actions: Compare the live GRC calendar record count to the obligations register maintained at fiscal-year start.
Investigate and resolve any obligation present in one but not the other.
Add newly identified obligations (new OSFI guideline, new jurisdiction) to both the register and the calendar.
Sign and date the reconciliation.
checklist.done: the calendar and the obligations register reconcile with a signed quarterly reconciliation.

checklist.step: Retain filing-timeliness evidence
actions: Move each closed obligation's confirmation, delivered document and reviewer sign-off into the compliance evidence repository under the fiscal year and obligation name.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by obligation, due date and confirmation number.
checklist.done: closed-obligation evidence is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and searchable in the repository.

checklist.step: Log exceptions for any missed or late filing
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every obligation filed after its due date, naming the obligation, due date, actual date and days late.
Assign a root cause (resourcing, data delay, unclear instruction) and a named owner for corrective action.
Set a remediation date and a control change to prevent recurrence.
Carry open exceptions into the next quarter's reconciliation as mandatory closure items.
checklist.done: every missed or late filing has a tracker issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and carried-forward status.

checklist.step: Governance review of calendar completeness and timeliness metrics
actions: Review the quarterly reconciliation, at-risk report and exception log at the risk committee.
Confirm the on-time filing rate and discuss any repeat root causes.
Approve any change to the obligations register, reminder cadence or owning-role assignments.
Record the committee's review and approval in the minutes.
checklist.done: the risk committee has reviewed and recorded its approval of the calendar's completeness and timeliness performance for the quarter.

checklist.step: Refresh the calendar procedure annually
actions: Re-read OSFI's current annual filing instructions and any new guideline or bulletin issued in the year.
Update the obligations register and procedure for any new, removed or changed obligation.
Route the updated procedure to the Chief Risk Officer for annual approval.
Publish the approved procedure and notify all preparers and reviewers of any change.
checklist.done: the procedure and obligations register are refreshed and re-approved before the new fiscal year's filing cycle begins.

testing.step: Build the population of calendar entries due in the test period
actions: Export from the GRC platform every calendar record with a due date inside the test quarter, including status and actual completion date.
Add any obligation identified in the obligations register but missing from the export.
Reconcile the extract count to the register and resolve any difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the obligations register and signed as complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of annual-return and AGM/board-notice items.
Take a random sample of 10 remaining entries, seeded and reproducible.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every annual-return and AGM-cycle entry.

testing.step: Re-perform the due-date computation for each sampled entry
actions: For each sampled entry, independently derive the due date from the statute, OSFI instruction or by-law provision cited.
Compare the derived date to the calendar's recorded due date; any mismatch is an exception.
For AGM items, recompute the 21-day notice window against the actual meeting date.
testing.done: each sampled entry's due date is independently re-derived and compared with no unexplained mismatch.

testing.step: Trace each sampled entry to submission or delivery evidence
actions: For OSFI filings, open the Internal Regulatory System and confirm the submission exists with the confirmation number recorded on the calendar record.
For board/AGM items, confirm the board portal shows the notice or report delivered on or before the recorded date.
Capture a screenshot of the system evidence into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled entry traces to real submission or delivery evidence matching the recorded date.

testing.step: Verify reminder rules actually fired
actions: Pull the alert delivery log for each sampled entry's T-60/T-30/T-10 (and T-21-day for AGM items) rules.
Confirm delivery timestamps align with the configured offsets from the due date.
Log any rule that failed to fire as an exception.
testing.done: reminder delivery logs confirm every configured rule fired at the correct offset for the sample.

testing.step: Test the appointed actuary's report timing on the sample
actions: For any sampled entry tied to the s. 368/369 report, confirm the delivery date to CEO/CFO precedes the calendar due date.
Where a s. 369 escalation was logged, confirm director and (if applicable) Superintendent notification is evidenced and dated.
Log as an exception any report delivered late or an unescalated material matter.
testing.done: actuary report timing and any required escalation are verified against the evidence for the sample.

testing.step: Recompute the on-time filing rate for the population
actions: Using the full population extract, recompute the count of entries with a positive (on-time or early) variance versus the calendar's own reported rate.
Investigate any difference between the recomputed and reported rate.
Note any entry closed without an evidence attachment as a control failure, independent of timeliness.
testing.done: the on-time filing rate is independently recomputed and reconciles to the reported rate, or the difference is explained.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception found in re-performance, evidence tracing or reminder testing.
Assign root cause and a named owner distinct from the original preparer.
Set a remediation date and confirm the item is added to next quarter's mandatory retest list.
testing.done: every test exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Independent reviewer signs the test workpaper
actions: Confirm the Internal Auditor performing the test authored none of the sampled calendar entries.
Review the population, sample, re-performance notes and exception log for completeness.
Sign and date the workpaper.
testing.done: the workpaper carries a dated sign-off from a reviewer independent of the sampled entries.

testing.step: Conclude and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for missed statutory deadlines.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) referencing the evidence.
Report results and any open breach to the risk committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Maintain the company's authorized-classes register
actions: In the Internal Regulatory System open the Company Authorizations module and enter the classes of insurance listed on the current OSFI order to commence and carry on business.
Add every jurisdiction where the company holds a Certificate of Authority, with its authorized lines and expiry/renewal date.
Attach a scanned copy of the OSFI order and each Certificate of Authority to the register entry.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm the register matches the source documents before it is published.
checklist.done: the register lists every authorized class per jurisdiction with the source document attached and counsel confirmation.

checklist.step: Gate new product or class launches on authorization verification
actions: When Product notifies a new class or jurisdiction launch, look up the class in the authorized-classes register.
If the class is not listed for the target jurisdiction, block the launch and open an OSFI new-class approval request or a Certificate of Authority application as applicable.
Record the gate decision (proceed / blocked pending approval) on the launch request.
Notify the Insurance Product Manager of the gate outcome and any required lead time.
checklist.done: every new class/jurisdiction launch has a recorded gate decision tied to the authorization register.

checklist.step: Submit OSFI approval requests for a new or changed authorized class
actions: Prepare the OSFI approval submission describing the new class, business rationale and expected volumes per s. 254/587.1/678.
Submit through the Internal Regulatory System and record the submission date and reference number.
Track OSFI's response and, on approval, update the register with the amended order and effective date.
Notify Distribution Operations Manager once the register is updated so the launch gate can be lifted.
checklist.done: the OSFI approval is submitted, tracked to decision, and the register reflects any amended order.

checklist.step: Apply for or renew state Certificates of Authority ahead of market entry
actions: Confirm with Distribution Operations Manager the target state and lines needed.
File the Certificate of Authority application (or line-of-authority amendment) with the state insurance department, attaching the required financial statements and biographical affidavits.
Track the application to approval and record the Certificate of Authority number and effective date in the register.
Flag any state requiring a certificate of deposit or trust fund as a pre-condition and route to Treasury.
checklist.done: each new-state application is tracked to an issued Certificate of Authority recorded in the register.

checklist.step: Verify authority before every underwriting submission is bound
actions: In the underwriting workstation, confirm the submission's class of business and risk state against the authorized-classes register before quoting.
Where the platform's authorization gate flags a mismatch, stop and escalate to Distribution Operations Manager rather than overriding.
Record the verification check on the submission file.
Bind only once the gate shows a verified, current authorization.
checklist.done: every bound submission carries a recorded, gate-verified authorization check.

checklist.step: Configure the underwriting platform authorization gate
actions: Load the authorized-classes register into the underwriting platform's rating/eligibility rules as a hard stop by class and state.
Test the gate with a known unauthorized class/state combination to confirm it blocks quoting.
Schedule a nightly sync from the Internal Regulatory System register to the platform gate.
Log any sync failure to IT Service Desk for same-day resolution.
checklist.done: the platform gate blocks unauthorized class/state combinations and syncs nightly from the register.

checklist.step: Monitor Certificate of Authority and OSFI order expiry/renewal dates
actions: Load every Certificate of Authority expiry date into the GRC platform's calendar with T-90/T-60/T-30 reminders.
File the renewal application before the T-30 reminder and track it to confirmation.
Update the register with the renewed certificate number and new expiry date.
Escalate any certificate approaching expiry with no filed renewal to Distribution Operations Manager.
checklist.done: no Certificate of Authority lapses without a tracked, filed renewal in the calendar.

checklist.step: Reconcile bound business to the authorized-classes register monthly
actions: Extract the prior month's bound policies from the underwriting platform by class and state.
Match each row to a current authorization in the register.
List unmatched rows for immediate investigation.
Report the reconciliation result to Distribution Operations Manager.
checklist.done: every bound policy for the month matches a current authorization or is listed as an exception.

checklist.step: Investigate and remediate any policy bound outside authorized scope
actions: For each unmatched policy, determine whether it was bound in a genuinely unauthorized class/jurisdiction or a register data error.
Where genuinely unauthorized, assess the need for a self-report to OSFI or the state regulator and prepare it.
Direct policy administration to non-renew or transfer the business as required.
Document the remediation decision and completion date.
checklist.done: every genuinely out-of-scope policy has a documented remediation decision, including any regulator self-report.

checklist.step: Log exceptions with root cause and disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every out-of-scope bind or register data error found.
Assign a root cause (gate override, stale register, missed sync) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and a control fix (e.g. removing override capability).
Carry open issues into the next monthly reconciliation as mandatory closure items.
checklist.done: every exception has a tracker issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and control fix.

checklist.step: Brief underwriting teams on authorized scope changes
actions: On any register update (new class, new state, expired certificate), issue a bulletin to affected underwriting teams.
Confirm the platform gate reflects the change before the bulletin is sent.
Track acknowledgement from each team lead.
File the bulletin and acknowledgements with the register update.
checklist.done: every register change is communicated to underwriting with tracked acknowledgement before it takes effect operationally.

checklist.step: Retain authorization evidence for the retention period
actions: Move OSFI order excerpts, Certificate of Authority copies and verification worksheets into the compliance evidence repository under jurisdiction and class.
Apply the 7-year-from-expiry-or-amendment retention label.
Confirm the repository index is searchable by jurisdiction, class and certificate number.
checklist.done: authorization evidence is filed, labelled for retention and searchable by jurisdiction and class.

checklist.step: Annual counsel review of the authority-to-write procedure
actions: Re-read the current OSFI order and every state Certificate of Authority against the register.
Update the procedure for any regulatory or business change.
Route the updated procedure for approval and republish.
Notify Distribution Operations Manager and UW Operations Manager of any change.
checklist.done: the procedure and register are refreshed and re-approved annually.

checklist.step: Report authorization status to governance
actions: Present the quarterly reconciliation results and any open exceptions to the compliance committee.
Highlight any jurisdiction with a certificate nearing expiry without a filed renewal.
Record committee feedback and any directed action.
File the presentation with the committee minutes.
checklist.done: the compliance committee has reviewed and recorded authorization status and any open exceptions for the quarter.

checklist.step: Test the authorization gate after every underwriting platform release
actions: After each platform release, re-run the known unauthorized class/state test case.
Confirm the gate still blocks quoting as designed.
Log any regression to the release team and hold the release from going live for underwriting until fixed.
Record the test result against the release ticket.
checklist.done: the authorization gate is verified functional after every platform release before go-live.

testing.step: Build the population of bound business for the test period
actions: Extract every policy bound in the quarter from the underwriting platform, by class of insurance and risk jurisdiction.
Reconcile the extract count to the underwriting platform's bind report for the quarter.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the platform's bind report and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the authorized-classes register
actions: Match every bound policy's class and jurisdiction to a current entry in the Internal Regulatory System register.
List unmatched rows as automatic exceptions, with no judgement applied.
Cross-check any newly opened class or jurisdiction in the period against a corresponding OSFI approval or Certificate of Authority.
testing.done: every bound policy is matched to a current authorization or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of policies bound in any class or jurisdiction opened in the test period.
Take a random sample of 20 additional rows, seeded and reproducible, from the remaining population.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every newly opened class or jurisdiction.

testing.step: Re-perform the authorization check for each sampled policy
actions: Open the Internal Regulatory System register and independently confirm the class/jurisdiction was authorized as of the bind date.
Compare to the platform gate's recorded verification; any difference is an exception.
Capture the register screen showing the authorization as of the bind date into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled policy's authorization is independently re-verified as of its bind date with captured evidence.

testing.step: Trace Certificate of Authority and OSFI order coverage for the sample
actions: For each sampled jurisdiction, pull the Certificate of Authority or OSFI order excerpt and confirm the class is listed.
Confirm the certificate/order was in force (not expired or amended out) on the bind date.
Log any lapsed or narrower authorization as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled policy traces to a Certificate of Authority or OSFI order in force for that class on the bind date.

testing.step: Recompute the register-to-platform sync timing
actions: For 10 sampled entries, compare the register update date for any authorization change to the date the underwriting platform gate reflected it.
Flag any gap where business could have bound before the gate was updated.
Confirm no policy in the sample was bound during such a gap.
testing.done: register-to-platform sync timing is confirmed to have prevented any bind during an update gap, or a breach is logged.

testing.step: Test the authorization gate control design
actions: Attempt to quote a known unauthorized class/state combination in a test environment.
Confirm the gate blocks the quote and no override path exists without a logged approval.
Log a control-design exception if the gate can be bypassed silently.
testing.done: the gate is confirmed to block unauthorized combinations without a silent override path.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with policy number, class, jurisdiction and the compliance impact.
Assign root cause and an owner distinct from the underwriter who bound the policy.
Set a remediation date and, for genuinely unauthorized business, confirm a self-report assessment was opened with Regulatory Counsel.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and self-report assessment where applicable.

testing.step: Independent reviewer sign-off
actions: Confirm the reviewer performed none of the sampled authorization verifications.
Review the population, sample, re-performance and exception log for completeness.
Sign and date the workpaper.
testing.done: a reviewer independent of the sample has signed and dated the workpaper.

testing.step: Conclude, report and file
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references and any required regulator self-report status.
Report to the compliance committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is reported to the committee and filed.

checklist.step: Intake the new producer record and open a verification worksheet
actions: In the agency/producer management system, create the producer record from the signed producer agreement and capture the NPN (National Producer Number).
Open a licensing verification worksheet recording the requested lines of authority and target solicitation states.
Set the producer record status to 'Pending Verification' so it cannot be used to bind business.
Notify the Broker Support Specialist that the producer is in intake.
checklist.done: the producer record exists with NPN captured and status held at 'Pending Verification'.

checklist.step: Verify the resident and non-resident license status via NIPR
actions: Log in to the NIPR Producer Database (PDB) and search by NPN.
Confirm the license status is Active for the resident state and each target non-resident state, and that the line of authority (Life, P&C, etc.) matches the intended solicitation.
Check for any regulatory action or CE deficiency flag on the record.
Print or export the PDB result and attach it to the verification worksheet with the pull date.
checklist.done: an active, line-matched license is confirmed in every target state with a dated PDB export attached.

checklist.step: Resolve any inactive, expired or line-mismatched license before proceeding
actions: Where the PDB shows an inactive or expired license, notify the producer and Broker Relationship Manager that solicitation cannot begin.
Where the line of authority does not cover the intended product, direct the producer to obtain the correct line before continuing intake.
Hold the producer record at 'Pending Verification' until the deficiency is cleared and re-verified in NIPR.
Log the deficiency and resolution date on the worksheet.
checklist.done: no producer record advances past 'Pending Verification' while a license deficiency remains open.

checklist.step: Confirm appointment eligibility before filing
actions: In NIPR, check the producer's appointment history for any existing termination-for-cause or regulatory bar with the company's group.
Confirm the producer has completed any required company-specific product or E&O training per the onboarding checklist.
Record the eligibility confirmation and training completion date on the worksheet.
Route the worksheet to the Producer Compliance Manager for the appointment-filing decision.
checklist.done: appointment eligibility, including no disqualifying history, is confirmed and recorded before filing.

checklist.step: Release the producer record for solicitation only after verification is complete
actions: Review the completed verification worksheet including PDB export and eligibility confirmation.
Change the producer record status to 'Active — Solicitation Authorized' in the agency/producer management system.
Set the authorized lines and states on the producer record to match the verified PDB scope exactly.
Notify the Broker Relationship Manager the producer may begin soliciting.
checklist.done: the producer record is set to solicitation-authorized only with the verified lines and states, and reviewer sign-off recorded.

checklist.step: File the company appointment with each state within the statutory window
actions: In NIPR, submit the appointment transaction for the company/producer/state combination, paying the appointment fee where required.
Record the submission date and confirmation number against the state's statutory filing window (commonly 15-30 days from date of first application/sale).
Confirm the appointment shows Active in the PDB once processed.
File the confirmation in the producer record.
checklist.done: the appointment is filed within the statutory window with an Active status confirmed in NIPR.

checklist.step: Configure a system gate blocking unverified producers from binding
actions: Load the agency/producer management system's authorized-producer feed into the underwriting platform's bind eligibility check.
Configure the platform to reject any bind attempt by a producer not flagged 'Active — Solicitation Authorized'.
Test the gate with a pending-verification producer ID and confirm it blocks the bind.
Schedule a nightly sync between the two systems.
checklist.done: the underwriting platform blocks binds from any producer not confirmed solicitation-authorized, verified by test.

checklist.step: Monitor for solicitation activity ahead of verification completion
actions: Run a weekly report of any quote or application activity tied to a producer record still marked 'Pending Verification'.
Investigate each hit with the Broker Relationship Manager and the producer directly.
Suspend the producer's system access immediately on confirmed unlicensed solicitation.
Log the finding for the exceptions process.
checklist.done: no unverified producer's solicitation activity goes uninvestigated for more than one week.

checklist.step: Track state appointment filing deadlines
actions: Load each state's statutory appointment filing deadline (from date of first application) into the GRC calendar.
Set a T-10-day reminder ahead of the deadline for any appointment not yet filed.
Escalate any appointment approaching its deadline unfiled to the Producer Compliance Manager.
Record the actual filing date against the deadline for variance tracking.
checklist.done: every appointment filing deadline is tracked with a T-10-day reminder and recorded actual filing date.

checklist.step: Investigate and remediate unlicensed solicitation findings
actions: Review each confirmed unlicensed-solicitation finding, including the dates of activity and the license gap.
Assess the need for a self-report to the affected state's insurance department.
Direct commission clawback or policy remediation as required by state rule.
Document the remediation decision and completion date.
checklist.done: every confirmed finding has a documented remediation decision including any regulator self-report.

checklist.step: Log exceptions with root cause and disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every unlicensed solicitation or late appointment filing found.
Assign root cause (intake gap, gate override, PDB data lag) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and confirm the corrective control change.
Carry open issues to the next quarterly test as mandatory retest items.
checklist.done: every exception has an issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and carried-forward retest status.

checklist.step: Reconcile producer count to NIPR appointment records monthly
actions: Extract the active producer count by state from the agency/producer management system.
Compare to the NIPR appointment roster for the same states.
Investigate any producer active in one system but not the other.
Report the reconciliation to Producer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: the agency system and NIPR appointment roster reconcile monthly with investigated differences.

checklist.step: Retain verification and appointment evidence
actions: Move PDB exports, verification worksheets and appointment confirmations into the compliance evidence repository under the producer's NPN.
Apply the 7-year-from-termination retention label.
Confirm the record is searchable by NPN, state and appointment date.
checklist.done: verification and appointment evidence is filed, labelled for retention and searchable by NPN.

checklist.step: Report producer licensing status to compliance governance
actions: Present the monthly reconciliation and any open unlicensed-solicitation findings to the compliance committee.
Highlight repeat root causes and any control gaps in the underwriting platform gate.
Record committee feedback and directed action.
File the presentation with the committee minutes.
checklist.done: the compliance committee has reviewed producer licensing status and open findings for the period.

checklist.step: Annual review of the verification procedure
actions: Re-read each state's producer licensing statute and NIPR PDB data specification for changes.
Update the procedure and gate configuration for any change.
Route the updated procedure for approval and republish to Licensing Ops.
Notify Broker Relationship Manager of any changed intake requirement.
checklist.done: the procedure is refreshed and re-approved annually against current state statutes and NIPR specifications.

testing.step: Build the population of producers onboarded or newly appointed in the period
actions: Extract every producer record created or moved to 'Active — Solicitation Authorized' status in the quarter.
Add every new state appointment filed in the quarter for existing producers.
Reconcile the extract to the onboarding log and resolve any difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the onboarding log and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to NIPR verification and appointment records
actions: Match each population row to a completed NIPR verification worksheet and, where filed, an appointment confirmation.
List unmatched rows as automatic exceptions with no judgement applied.
testing.done: every population row is matched to verification and appointment evidence or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of producers with any solicitation-activity-before-verification flag raised in the period.
Take a random sample of 25 additional rows, seeded and reproducible, from the remaining population.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every flagged early-solicitation producer.

testing.step: Re-verify license status in NIPR for each sampled producer
actions: Independently pull the NIPR PDB record for each sampled NPN as of the solicitation start date, using PDB history where available.
Confirm the license was active with the matching line of authority on that date.
Compare to the worksheet's recorded finding; any difference is an exception.
Capture the PDB screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled producer's license status as of the solicitation start date is independently confirmed with captured evidence.

testing.step: Trace solicitation start dates to the producer record status change
actions: Pull the first quote or application date for each sampled producer from underwriting or CRM records.
Compare to the date the producer record was set to 'Active — Solicitation Authorized'.
Log as an exception any solicitation activity dated before the authorization status change.
testing.done: no sampled producer shows solicitation activity before their authorization status change, or the breach is logged.

testing.step: Verify appointment filing timeliness for the sample
actions: For each sampled appointment, compute the statutory filing deadline from the recorded first-application date.
Confirm the NIPR appointment submission date is on or before that deadline.
Log any late filing as an exception with the number of days late.
testing.done: appointment filing timeliness is independently recomputed for every sampled appointment.

testing.step: Test the underwriting platform bind-eligibility gate
actions: In a test environment, attempt a bind using a producer ID flagged 'Pending Verification'.
Confirm the platform rejects the bind with no override path outside a logged exception process.
Log a control-design exception if the gate can be bypassed.
testing.done: the bind-eligibility gate is confirmed to block unverified producers without a silent override.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with producer NPN, state, gap dates and compliance impact.
Assign root cause and an owner distinct from the original verifier.
Set a remediation date and confirm any self-report assessment opened with Regulatory Counsel for confirmed unlicensed solicitation.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and self-report status where applicable.

testing.step: Independent reviewer sign-off
actions: Confirm the reviewer performed none of the sampled verifications.
Review the population, sample, re-performance notes and exception log for completeness.
Sign and date the workpaper.
testing.done: a reviewer independent of the sample has signed and dated the workpaper.

testing.step: Conclude, report and file
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for pre-verification solicitation.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Report to the compliance committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is reported and filed.

checklist.step: Identify the triggering event for each appointment or termination
actions: For a new appointment, record the date of the producer's first application or sale that triggers the filing window.
For a termination, record the last date of association (contract end date or for-cause discovery date).
Enter the triggering date and transaction type into the agency/producer management system record.
Notify the Broker Relationship Manager of the transaction opening.
checklist.done: every appointment or termination record shows a triggering date and transaction type.

checklist.step: Compute the statutory filing window for the transaction state
actions: Look up the target state's statutory appointment or termination filing window from the licensing procedure's state matrix.
Compute the due date as trigger date plus the statutory window.
Enter the due date onto the transaction record.
Flag any state matrix entry not refreshed in the last 12 months for re-verification.
checklist.done: every transaction has a computed due date sourced from a current state matrix entry.

checklist.step: File the appointment transaction in NIPR
actions: In NIPR, submit the appointment transaction for the company/producer/state, paying the fee where required.
Capture the confirmation number and submission timestamp.
Confirm the appointment shows Active in the PDB.
Record the confirmation against the due date for variance tracking.
checklist.done: the appointment is filed with a captured confirmation number and confirmed Active status.

checklist.step: File the termination transaction in NIPR
actions: In NIPR, submit the termination transaction, selecting the correct reason code (voluntary, for cause, non-renewal).
For a for-cause termination, complete the required narrative field describing the conduct basis.
Capture the confirmation number and submission timestamp.
Update the producer record status to Terminated with the effective date.
checklist.done: the termination is filed with the correct reason code and, where for cause, a completed narrative and confirmation captured.

checklist.step: Draft and clear the for-cause termination narrative through counsel
actions: Review the underlying investigation or conduct finding supporting the for-cause termination.
Draft or edit the narrative for factual accuracy and to avoid unsupported characterizations.
Approve the narrative for filing and record the approval date.
Advise on any parallel notification obligation (e.g. to a reinsurer or MGA agreement counterparty).
checklist.done: every for-cause narrative is counsel-reviewed and approved before it is filed in NIPR.

checklist.step: Notify affected business units of the appointment or termination
actions: On appointment confirmation, notify underwriting and commissions that the producer may transact business in the state.
On termination, notify underwriting to block new business submissions from the producer effective the termination date.
Confirm commission payments are stopped or adjusted per the termination date.
Record notification completion on the transaction file.
checklist.done: underwriting and commissions are notified and system access adjusted consistent with the transaction's effective date.

checklist.step: Track transactions approaching their statutory due date
actions: Load every open transaction's due date into the GRC calendar with a T-5-business-day reminder.
Review the at-risk report daily for transactions inside the reminder window still unfiled.
Escalate any transaction that will miss its due date to the Producer Compliance Manager the same day.
Record the escalation and any expedited filing action taken.
checklist.done: every open transaction is tracked with a T-5-day reminder and same-day escalation on at-risk items.

checklist.step: Reconcile filed transactions to the agency/producer management system
actions: Weekly, compare the NIPR filing log to the agency/producer management system's open transaction list.
Confirm every filed transaction is marked closed in the agency system with the confirmation number attached.
Investigate any transaction filed in NIPR but not reflected in the agency system, or vice versa.
checklist.done: the NIPR filing log and agency system reconcile weekly with investigated differences.

checklist.step: Investigate and remediate any transaction filed outside its window
actions: For each late transaction, determine the root cause (queue backlog, missing information, system outage).
Assess whether a late for-cause termination report requires a self-disclosure to the state.
Direct process or staffing corrections to prevent recurrence.
Document the remediation decision and completion date.
checklist.done: every late transaction has a documented root cause and remediation decision, including any required self-disclosure.

checklist.step: Log exceptions with root cause and disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every transaction filed outside its statutory window.
Assign root cause and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and a control fix.
Carry open issues into the next quarterly test as mandatory retest items.
checklist.done: every exception has an issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and carried-forward retest status.

checklist.step: Retain appointment and termination evidence
actions: Move NIPR confirmations and for-cause narratives into the compliance evidence repository under the producer's NPN and state.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the transaction date.
Confirm searchability by NPN, state, transaction type and filing date.
checklist.done: transaction evidence is filed, labelled for retention and searchable by NPN and transaction type.

checklist.step: Report timeliness performance to compliance governance
actions: Present the quarter's on-time filing rate and any for-cause termination reports to the compliance committee.
Highlight any repeat root cause behind late filings.
Record committee feedback and directed action.
File the presentation with the committee minutes.
checklist.done: the compliance committee has reviewed timeliness performance and for-cause reports for the quarter.

checklist.step: Maintain the state statutory-window matrix
actions: Annually, or on a known statute change, re-read each state's appointment and termination filing window statute.
Update the state matrix with the current window and its citation.
Route the updated matrix to Producer Licensing Coordinator and publish.
Note any state that shortened its window for immediate procedure update.
checklist.done: the state matrix is refreshed with current statutory windows and citations at least annually.

checklist.step: Audit trail check on producer status changes
actions: Monthly, review the agency/producer management system's audit log for any status change made outside the standard appointment/termination workflow.
Investigate any direct status edit not tied to a filed NIPR transaction.
Correct unauthorized edits and restrict access as needed.
Log the review outcome.
checklist.done: monthly audit log review finds no unauthorized producer status changes, or each is investigated and corrected.

checklist.step: Confirm terminated producers cannot re-enter the bind-eligible pool without new verification
actions: Confirm the underwriting platform's bind-eligibility feed reflects terminated status the same business day as the NIPR filing.
Test that a terminated producer's ID is rejected at bind.
Require a fresh licensing verification worksheet before any terminated producer is reappointed.
Log the test result.
checklist.done: terminated producers are blocked from binding and require full re-verification before reappointment.

testing.step: Build the population of appointment and termination transactions for the period
actions: Extract every appointment and termination transaction filed in the quarter from the NIPR filing log.
Add any transaction opened but not yet filed as of quarter end, noting its status.
Reconcile the extract to the agency/producer management system's transaction list.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the agency system's transaction list and signed as complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the method
actions: Take 100% of for-cause terminations.
Take a random sample of 25 additional transactions, seeded and reproducible, from remaining appointments and terminations.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every for-cause termination.

testing.step: Recompute the statutory due date for each sampled transaction
actions: Independently look up the applicable state's statutory window from the current statute text, not the internal matrix.
Recompute the due date from the recorded trigger date.
Compare to the matrix-derived due date used at filing time; log any discrepancy.
testing.done: the statutory due date is independently recomputed for every sampled transaction and compared to the matrix value.

testing.step: Trace each sampled transaction's filing date in NIPR
actions: Open NIPR and pull the actual filing timestamp and confirmation number for each sampled transaction.
Compare the filing date to the recomputed due date; any filing after the due date is an exception.
Capture the NIPR confirmation screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled transaction's actual filing date is compared to the recomputed due date with captured evidence.

testing.step: Review for-cause termination narratives for counsel approval
actions: For each sampled for-cause termination, confirm a dated counsel approval exists that pre-dates the NIPR filing.
Read the filed narrative and confirm it matches the approved version.
Log as an exception any filed narrative that was not counsel-approved or was materially altered after approval.
testing.done: every sampled for-cause narrative is confirmed counsel-approved and unaltered before filing, or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Verify system access changes align with termination effective dates
actions: For each sampled termination, pull the underwriting platform access log for the terminated producer.
Confirm bind eligibility was revoked on or before the termination effective date.
Log any gap where the producer retained bind eligibility after termination as an exception.
testing.done: bind eligibility revocation is confirmed to align with or precede the termination effective date for every sampled row.

testing.step: Recompute the population's on-time filing rate
actions: Using the full population extract, independently recompute the percentage of transactions filed within their statutory window.
Compare to the rate reported by Producer Licensing Coordinator; investigate any difference.
Confirm every for-cause termination in the population was filed on time with zero exceptions tolerated.
testing.done: the on-time filing rate is independently recomputed and reconciles, with zero late for-cause terminations confirmed.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with transaction type, state, days late and compliance impact.
Assign root cause and an owner distinct from the original filer.
Set a remediation date and confirm any required state self-disclosure was opened for late for-cause reports.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and self-disclosure status where applicable.

testing.step: Independent reviewer sign-off
actions: Confirm the reviewer processed none of the sampled transactions.
Review the population, sample, re-performance notes and exception log for completeness.
Sign and date the workpaper.
testing.done: a reviewer independent of the sample has signed and dated the workpaper.

testing.step: Conclude, report and file
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for late for-cause terminations.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Report to the compliance committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is reported and filed.

checklist.step: Build the renewal calendar from current license expiry dates
actions: Pull each producer's current license expiry date and CE cycle end date from the NIPR PDB.
Load the dates into the agency/producer management system's renewal log, one row per producer per state.
Cross-check the loaded dates against the state's published renewal cycle (typically biennial, tied to birth month or license anniversary).
Flag any producer missing an expiry date for immediate follow-up.
checklist.done: the renewal log carries a current expiry date and CE cycle end date for every producer/state combination.

checklist.step: Configure renewal and CE reminder alerts
actions: Set T-90/T-60/T-30 reminder rules against each renewal log row, addressed to the producer and the Broker Relationship Manager.
Add a CE-hours-outstanding reminder at T-45 for any producer below the required hour count.
Test-fire one reminder of each type and confirm delivery.
Escalate any non-firing rule to the Producer Licensing Coordinator's manager for fix.
checklist.done: every renewal log row has active, tested reminder rules including a CE-specific alert.

checklist.step: Monitor CE hour completion against state requirements
actions: Pull the CE completion status field from the NIPR PDB for each producer approaching renewal.
Compare completed hours to the state's required hour count and topic mix (e.g. ethics hours).
Where the producer's own course provider reports directly to the state, confirm the state's CE tracking system shows the same completed hours.
Record any shortfall on the renewal log row with the outstanding hour count.
checklist.done: CE completion status is confirmed against state requirements for every producer approaching renewal, with shortfalls recorded.

checklist.step: Validate CE course provider accreditation and topic relevance
actions: Where a producer self-reports CE completion outside the NIPR-fed provider network, look up the course provider in the state's approved-provider list.
Confirm the course topic and hour count map to the state's required curriculum (e.g. ethics hours, flood/long-term-care specific hours where mandated).
Reject and require re-completion of any course from an unapproved provider or with a mismatched topic code.
Record the validation outcome on the renewal log row.
checklist.done: every self-reported CE completion is validated against an approved provider and the correct topic/hour requirement before it is accepted.

checklist.step: Notify producers of upcoming renewal and CE shortfalls
actions: On each T-90/T-60/T-30 alert, send the producer a notice naming the expiry date and any outstanding CE hours.
Provide the producer with the state's approved CE provider list if hours are short.
Log the notice sent and the producer's response.
Escalate non-responsive producers to Producer Licensing Coordinator at T-30.
checklist.done: every producer approaching renewal receives a dated notice, with escalation logged for non-response by T-30.

checklist.step: Verify renewal completion in NIPR before the expiry date
actions: Re-pull the PDB record at T-10 to confirm the renewal has been processed and the license status remains Active with a new expiry date.
Where renewal is not yet reflected, contact the producer for confirmation of submission to the state.
Update the renewal log with the new expiry date once confirmed.
Close the renewal log row only when the new expiry date is captured.
checklist.done: every renewal is confirmed processed in the PDB with a new expiry date before the prior license expires.

checklist.step: Suspend solicitation eligibility immediately on a lapsed license
actions: Where the T-10 PDB check shows a license still not renewed by the expiry date, change the producer record status to 'Suspended — License Lapsed' the same business day.
Confirm the underwriting platform's bind-eligibility feed reflects the suspension before end of day.
Notify underwriting and commissions to hold all new business from the producer.
Log the suspension date and reason.
checklist.done: solicitation eligibility is suspended and the bind gate updated the same business day a license lapses.

checklist.step: Process reinstatement once renewal and CE are confirmed
actions: Re-pull the PDB record once the producer reports renewal completion and confirm Active status and CE hours met.
Change the producer record status back to 'Active — Solicitation Authorized' only on confirmed Active PDB status.
Notify underwriting the suspension is lifted.
Record the reinstatement date on the renewal log.
checklist.done: reinstatement occurs only after PDB confirms Active status and CE completion, with the date recorded.

checklist.step: Investigate any solicitation activity during a lapsed period
actions: Pull the producer's quote/application activity for the lapsed-license window from underwriting records.
Where activity is found, assess the need for a self-report to the state and any policy remediation.
Direct commission clawback for business written during the lapse where required.
Document the remediation decision.
checklist.done: any solicitation activity during a lapse is investigated with a documented remediation decision.

checklist.step: Reconcile the renewal log to NIPR monthly
actions: Compare the renewal log's expiry dates and status to a fresh NIPR PDB pull for the full active producer roster.
Investigate any mismatch, including producers active in the log but showing lapsed in NIPR.
Correct the log and report the reconciliation outcome to Producer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: the renewal log reconciles to NIPR monthly with investigated and corrected mismatches.

checklist.step: Log exceptions with root cause and disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every lapsed-license suspension and any confirmed lapse-period solicitation.
Assign root cause and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and a process fix where the reminder cadence failed.
Carry open issues into the next quarterly test as mandatory retest items.
checklist.done: every exception has an issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and carried-forward retest status.

checklist.step: Retain renewal and CE evidence
actions: Move PDB pulls, CE completion certificates and suspension/reinstatement records into the compliance evidence repository under NPN and renewal cycle.
Apply the 7-year retention label from termination.
Confirm searchability by NPN, state and expiry date.
checklist.done: renewal and CE evidence is filed, labelled for retention and searchable by NPN and expiry date.

checklist.step: Report renewal and suspension metrics to compliance governance
actions: Present the quarter's renewal on-time rate, CE shortfall count and suspensions to the compliance committee.
Highlight any producer segment with recurring lapses.
Record committee feedback and directed action.
File the presentation with the committee minutes.
checklist.done: the compliance committee has reviewed renewal and suspension metrics for the quarter.

checklist.step: Maintain the state CE requirement reference
actions: Annually re-read each state's CE hour and topic requirement.
Update the reference table used by Producer Licensing Coordinator.
Route for approval and publish.
Flag any state change requiring immediate reminder cadence adjustment.
checklist.done: the CE requirement reference is refreshed and re-approved at least annually.

checklist.step: Audit renewal log completeness against the full appointed-producer roster
actions: Quarterly, compare the renewal log's producer/state rows to the full appointed-producer roster from NIPR.
Add any missing producer/state row and investigate why it was omitted.
Report the completeness check result to the compliance committee.
Document the check date and outcome.
checklist.done: the renewal log is confirmed complete against the full appointed-producer roster each quarter.

testing.step: Build the population of licenses due for renewal in the period

testing.step: Re-verify renewal completion timing in NIPR for each sampled row

testing.step: Re-verify CE hour completion for each sampled row

Compare the revocation timestamp to the license expiry date; any gap where the producer could still bind is an exception.

testing.step: Verify reinstatement evidence for the sample

testing.step: Recompute the population's on-time renewal rate

Confirm the count of confirmed lapse-period solicitations matches the exceptions log.
testing.done: the on-time renewal rate is independently recomputed and reconciles to the reported rate.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date

Assign root cause and an owner distinct from the original processor.
Set a remediation date and confirm any required self-report assessment opened with Regulatory Counsel.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and self-report status where applicable.

testing.step: Independent reviewer sign-off

Review the population, sample, re-performance notes and exception log for completeness.
Sign and date the workpaper.
testing.done: a reviewer independent of the sample has signed and dated the workpaper.

testing.step: Conclude, report and file

Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Report to the compliance committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.

checklist.step: Disclose the screening requirement before the conditional offer is finalized
actions: Attach the background screening and 18 U.S.C. §1033 consent disclosure to every conditional offer for a role engaging in the business of insurance.
Confirm the candidate acknowledges the disclosure in the HRIS onboarding task before the offer is countersigned.
Flag any role unclear on 1033 applicability to Compliance Analyst for a scoping determination.
Record the disclosure acknowledgement date in the candidate's HRIS record.
checklist.done: every conditional offer for an in-scope role carries a recorded, acknowledged screening disclosure.

checklist.step: Capture signed consent for the background check
actions: Issue the FCRA-compliant background check authorization form through the HRIS onboarding workflow.
Confirm the candidate's electronic signature is captured before the request is submitted to the screening vendor.
Attach the signed consent to the candidate's HRIS file.
Block progression to the next onboarding step until consent is on file.
checklist.done: a signed background check consent is on file in HRIS before any screen is ordered.

checklist.step: Order and receive the background check
actions: Submit the screening request to the credit/background data service specifying criminal history, and where applicable financial/credit history for roles with fiduciary access.
Set the scope to cover felony convictions under state and federal law relevant to 18 U.S.C. §1033 (dishonesty, breach of trust, felony conviction).
Retrieve the completed report and log the receipt date in the screening tracker.
Route any 'Consider' or 'Flag' result to Compliance Analyst adjudication before allowing onboarding to continue.
checklist.done: the background check is ordered with the correct scope and its result logged before onboarding proceeds.

checklist.step: Adjudicate a clean result and clear the candidate
actions: Confirm the background report shows no disqualifying felony conviction and no unresolved flag.
Mark the candidate's screening status 'Cleared' in the tracker.
Release the HRIS onboarding workflow to proceed to start-date confirmation.
Notify the hiring manager the candidate is cleared to start.
checklist.done: a clean-result candidate is marked cleared and released to start only after this check.

checklist.step: Adjudicate a flagged conviction and determine 1033 applicability
actions: Review the flagged conviction against the felony categories covered by 18 U.S.C. §1033.
Determine whether the individual requires a written 1033 consent from the applicable state insurance regulator before engaging in the business of insurance.
Consult Regulatory Counsel on any ambiguous conviction category or lookback period question.
Document the applicability determination and next step (proceed, require consent application, decline).
checklist.done: every flagged conviction has a documented 1033 applicability determination signed by Head of Compliance.

checklist.step: Prepare and submit the 1033 consent application where required
actions: Prepare the written consent application to the appropriate state insurance regulator, including the conviction details, rehabilitation evidence and the role's duties.
Submit the application per the regulator's specified process and record the submission date.
Track the application to a written approval or denial.
File the regulator's response with the candidate's screening record.
checklist.done: a 1033 consent application, where required, is submitted and tracked to a written regulator response.

checklist.step: Hold the start date until consent or clearance is confirmed
actions: Keep the HRIS onboarding workflow at 'Pending Screening' status until either a 'Cleared' screening result or an approved 1033 consent is attached.
Confirm system access provisioning is not triggered until the workflow status changes.
Coordinate with the hiring manager to adjust the start date if screening or consent is not yet complete.
Log the actual start date against the clearance/consent date.
checklist.done: no candidate's start date precedes a confirmed screening clearance or approved 1033 consent, logged in HRIS.

checklist.step: Extend screening to newly contracted producers, not only employees
actions: Confirm the producer onboarding intake includes the same background screening and 1033 disclosure steps as employee hiring.
Coordinate with Producer Licensing Coordinator so the license verification and background screen complete before the producer record is set to solicitation-authorized.
Log the producer's screening status alongside their licensing verification worksheet.
Escalate any producer without a completed screen found active in the agency system.
checklist.done: every newly contracted producer's screening status is tracked alongside licensing verification before authorization.

checklist.step: Decline or terminate where consent is denied or unattainable
actions: Where the regulator denies the 1033 consent application, direct HR to rescind the offer or, for an existing employee, initiate separation from insurance-related duties.
Confirm system access is revoked the same day as the decision.
Document the decision, date and the individual's reassignment or separation.
Notify Regulatory Counsel to close out any open consent application file.
checklist.done: a denied or unattainable consent results in same-day access revocation and a documented separation or reassignment.

checklist.step: Monitor active employees and producers for new disqualifying events
actions: Run an annual re-screen for roles with ongoing fiduciary or licensing responsibility, per the procedure's re-screen schedule.
Monitor internal HR conduct/disciplinary records and producer E&O/regulatory action feeds for new disqualifying events.
Route any new event through the same adjudication and 1033-applicability process.
Log the monitoring cycle completion date.
checklist.done: an annual re-screen cycle runs for in-scope roles and new disqualifying events are routed through adjudication.

checklist.step: Reconcile onboarding starts to completed screenings monthly
actions: Extract every individual who started work in the month from HRIS.
Match each to a 'Cleared' screening status or approved 1033 consent dated before the start date.
List unmatched rows for immediate investigation and report to Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every monthly start is matched to a pre-dated clearance or consent, or listed as an exception.

checklist.step: Log exceptions with root cause and disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every individual who started before a completed screen or consent.
Assign root cause (workflow bypass, vendor delay, missed disclosure) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and a control fix.
Carry open issues into the next quarterly test as mandatory retest items.
checklist.done: every exception has an issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and carried-forward retest status.

checklist.step: Retain screening and consent evidence
actions: Move signed consent forms, background reports and any 1033 consent applications/approvals into the compliance evidence repository under the individual's employee or producer ID.
Apply the 7-year-from-separation retention label.
Confirm the record is access-restricted given its sensitive personal content and searchable only by authorized compliance staff.
checklist.done: screening and consent evidence is filed, access-restricted, labelled for retention and searchable by ID.

checklist.step: Report screening compliance to governance
actions: Present the quarter's screening completion rate, flagged-conviction count and 1033 consent outcomes to the compliance committee.
Highlight any exception involving a start before clearance.
Record committee feedback and directed action.
File the presentation with the committee minutes.
checklist.done: the compliance committee has reviewed screening compliance metrics for the quarter.

checklist.step: Annual review of the screening procedure
actions: Re-read 18 U.S.C. §1033 guidance and any state-specific background check or ban-the-box law affecting the screening scope.
Update the procedure and adjudication criteria for any change.
Route the updated procedure for Head of Compliance approval and republish.
Notify HR and Compliance Analyst of any changed requirement.
checklist.done: the procedure is refreshed and re-approved annually against current federal and state requirements.

testing.step: Build the population of individuals onboarded in the period
actions: Extract every new hire, transfer into an in-scope role, and newly contracted producer with a start date in the quarter.
Reconcile the extract to the HRIS onboarding log and the agency/producer management system's new-producer list.
Resolve any count difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to HRIS and the agency system and signed as complete.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the method
actions: Take 100% of individuals with a flagged background result or a 1033 consent application in the period.
Take a random sample of 20 additional rows, seeded and reproducible, from the remaining population.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers every flagged or 1033-consent case.

testing.step: Verify consent and screening completion pre-dates the start date
actions: For each sampled individual, pull the signed consent date, background check completion date and, where applicable, 1033 consent approval date from HRIS and the compliance evidence repository.
Compare each date to the recorded start date; any date on or after the start date is an exception.
Capture the HRIS record and evidence repository entry into the workpaper.
testing.done: consent and clearance dates are independently confirmed to pre-date the start date for every sampled individual.

testing.step: Re-perform the adjudication for sampled flagged results
actions: For each sampled flagged background result, independently review the report against the 18 U.S.C. §1033 disqualifying-felony categories.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded adjudication; log any difference as an exception.
Confirm the Head of Compliance sign-off is dated and present for each adjudication.
testing.done: adjudication of every sampled flagged result is independently re-performed and compared with a confirmed sign-off.

testing.step: Trace 1033 consent applications to regulator approval
actions: For each sampled 1033 case, confirm the consent application was submitted to the correct state regulator with complete conviction details.
Confirm a written approval is on file dated before the individual began engaging in the business of insurance.
Log as an exception any case where the individual began work before a written approval was received.
testing.done: every sampled 1033 case traces to a written regulator approval pre-dating the individual's start of insurance-related duties.

testing.step: Verify system access provisioning timing
actions: Pull the system access provisioning timestamp for each sampled individual from the IAM platform.
Compare to the screening clearance or 1033 approval date; any provisioning before clearance is an exception.
Confirm the HRIS onboarding workflow gate is configured to block provisioning as designed.
testing.done: system access provisioning is confirmed to follow, not precede, clearance for every sampled individual.

testing.step: Recompute the population's clearance-before-start rate
actions: Using the full population extract, independently recompute the percentage of individuals with clearance or consent dated before their start date.
Compare to the rate reported by Compliance Analyst; investigate any difference.
Confirm the count of confirmed early starts matches the exceptions log.
testing.done: the clearance-before-start rate is independently recomputed and reconciles to the reported rate.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with individual ID, gap in days and compliance impact.
Assign root cause and an owner distinct from the original screener.
Set a remediation date and confirm any required regulator notification was assessed with Regulatory Counsel.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and notification status where applicable.

testing.step: Independent reviewer sign-off
actions: Confirm the reviewer adjudicated none of the sampled screenings.
Review the population, sample, re-performance notes and exception log for completeness.
Sign and date the workpaper.
testing.done: a reviewer independent of the sample has signed and dated the workpaper.

testing.step: Conclude, report and file
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for starts before clearance.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Report to the compliance committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate is reported and filed.

checklist.step: Export the internal active producer roster

Save the export with a quarter-end timestamp in the reconciliation working folder.
Log the export row count.
checklist.done: the internal roster export is complete, timestamped and its row count logged.

Flag any producer record with an unresolvable NPN to Producer Licensing Coordinator before the match runs.

checklist.done: NPN and state fields are cleansed and standardized, with unresolvable records flagged before matching begins.

checklist.done: the NIPR appointment export is complete, matches the internal export's as-of date, and its row count is logged.

checklist.step: Match the two rosters by NPN and state

Update the reconciliation report with the resolution.
checklist.done: every internal-only break results in either a confirmed pending filing or an immediate suspension and corrective filing.

checklist.step: Investigate every NIPR-only break
actions: For each producer appointed in NIPR but not active internally, determine whether the internal record was never created, was incorrectly terminated, or the appointment should have been terminated in NIPR.
Where the appointment should be terminated, file the NIPR termination transaction and record the reason.
Where the internal record is missing in error, create it and set the correct status.
Update the reconciliation report with the resolution.
checklist.done: every NIPR-only break is resolved with either a filed termination or a corrected internal record.

checklist.step: Confirm bind eligibility is consistent with the reconciled status
actions: For every internal-only break suspended during investigation, confirm the underwriting platform's bind-eligibility feed reflects the suspension.
For every resolved break, confirm the platform's feed is updated to the corrected status within one business day.
Spot-check five resolved rows in the platform to confirm the feed sync.
Log any feed lag found.
checklist.done: bind eligibility in the underwriting platform is confirmed consistent with every reconciled producer status.

checklist.step: Check for solicitation activity during any internal-only break window

Where activity is found before appointment, assess the need for a self-report to the state.
Document the assessment outcome and any filed self-report.
Direct commission or policy remediation as required.
checklist.done: solicitation activity during any break window is checked, with a documented remediation decision including any self-report.

checklist.step: Finalize the quarterly reconciliation report
actions: Review the draft reconciliation report with all breaks resolved and documented.
Confirm the resolution timeline for each break is within the 15-business-day standard.
Sign and date the final reconciliation report.
File the report with supporting exports in the reconciliation working folder.
checklist.done: a signed, finalized reconciliation report with all breaks resolved within 15 business days exists for the quarter.

checklist.step: Track reconciliation cycle timeliness
actions: Load the reconciliation start deadline (quarter end + 5 business days) and resolution deadline (+ 15 business days) into the GRC calendar.
Set reminders at each milestone.
Record actual start and completion dates against the deadlines.
Escalate to Producer Compliance Manager any cycle at risk of missing the 15-business-day resolution standard.
checklist.done: every reconciliation cycle's start and completion is tracked against its calendar milestones with escalation on risk.

checklist.step: Log exceptions with root cause and disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for every break, whether internal-only or NIPR-only.
Assign root cause (filing delay, data entry error, missed termination) and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and confirm the corrective filing or record fix is complete.
Carry any unresolved break past 15 business days into escalation as a control failure.
checklist.done: every break has a tracker issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and resolution status.

checklist.step: Retain reconciliation evidence
actions: Move the signed reconciliation report, source exports and break-resolution notes into the compliance evidence repository under the quarter.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the record is searchable by quarter and by NPN for any producer with a break.
checklist.done: reconciliation evidence is filed, labelled for retention and searchable by quarter and NPN.

checklist.step: Report reconciliation results to compliance governance

Record committee feedback and directed action.
File the presentation with the committee minutes.

checklist.step: Improve upstream controls where breaks repeat
